test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 14 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

**A person who is unable to pay their debts.**
solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Bankrupt .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **Bankrupt** refers to a person who is legally declared unable to pay their debts.
 
• While **Debtor** is someone who owes money, it does not necessarily imply insolvency.
 
• **Pauper** denotes a very poor person, but it does not directly refer to someone unable to pay debts.
 
• **Insolvent** is a similar term, but "Bankrupt" is the more specific one-word substitute in this case.

Correct sentence: *The correct one-word substitute for a person who is unable to pay their debts is **Bankrupt**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bankrupt:**
 
 
• Legally declared unable to pay debts.
 
• Often involves a legal process to resolve financial obligations.
 
 
 
• **Debtor:**
 
 
• A person who owes money.
 
• Does not necessarily imply financial insolvency.
 
 
 
• **Pauper:**
 
 
• A very poor person.
 
• Does not directly mean inability to pay debts.
 
 
 
• **Insolvent:**
 
 
• Unable to pay debts, but broader than "Bankrupt."
 
• May not involve a legal declaration.
 
 
</ul
